content.text:
I added `src/lib/dayViewCache.ts`, and the day-view route now returns a Redis-cached copy of its response for 30 seconds. The cache is keyed per practitioner, in the form `clinic:dayview:<practitionerId>:<generation>:<day>`. No patient ids appear in keys, and every key expires within 15 minutes. `npm run verify` passes (typecheck and all 18 existing tests), but I did not add a test for the revoke path, so that behaviour is untested.

`POST /api/admin/care-team/revoke` now bumps that practitioner's generation counter. The revoked patient drops out of the next day-view call, and a read already in flight can't write back a stale entry.

The cached value is the endpoint's existing response, which includes patient ids and names. It has no visit reasons or notes, but it does mean patient names sit in Redis for up to 30 seconds. Because of that 30-second cache, a new or cancelled appointment can take up to 30 seconds to show in the day view.
